name: opencode

spawn.$comment-cwdMode: QUIRK: resolves its project from $PWD, not the spawn cwd. The watcher MUST set env.PWD and spawn with cwd inside the target repo, or it will silently analyse the wrong repository and answer confidently about it.

$comment-authSignatures: The first two are opencode's own wording. The rest are what an upstream API relayed through opencode reports when the credential behind it is revoked or has no route for the requested model: the error event carries `auth_unavailable` / `authentication_error` / `invalidated oauth token`, or `No available channel for model <name> under group default`. Without them every such attempt reads as a generic provider stream error, no pool is benched, and the next attempt picks another pool backed by the same dead credential. The same four phrases are DEFAULT_AUTH_SIGNATURES in src/lib/auth-signatures.js, which every connector gets on a provider stream error; they are declared here as well so they also apply to this connector's plain-output and stderr fast-fail paths.
$comment-quotaSignatures: empty on purpose: provider quota errors reach opencode from the upstream API in generic form (insufficient_quota, rate limit exceeded, too many requests), which DEFAULT_QUOTA_SIGNATURES in src/lib/quota.js already matches.

eventStream.$comment-usage: verified 2026-09-20 against opencode 1.18.31 and tests/fixtures/streams/opencode-hello.jsonl, a real capture of `opencode run --model hetzner/Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 --format json 'Reply with the single word ok.'`: each model step ends with a `step_finish` event whose `part.tokens` carries input/output/reasoning plus cache.read/cache.write. The counters are disjoint — the real session rows in opencode.db prove `total` = input + output + reasoning + cache.read + cache.write (tokens_input 368554 next to tokens_cache_read 1597440 on the same row) — so input is already the fresh class and no cache or reasoning subtraction applies. One step_finish arrives per model request; the rule sums them the same way opencode.db sums its per-message rows into the session totals. `part.cost` is deliberately unmapped: opencode reports 0 for relay models it has no price book for, and that zero is unknown, not free. The snapshot scan from earlier the same day (131 JSONL files, zero stream-*.jsonl) is superseded by this capture; do not treat a missing stream capture as zero usage.

$comment-auto: --auto is required for headless workflow dispatch: task files live under ~/.bullswarm, outside the target repo, and OpenCode otherwise pauses for an interactive permission approval. This template intentionally leaves --model unset so a plain OpenCode installation uses its own default; a provider that clones it pins --model <providerId>/<model> for its own pools, after which modelSelection can replace it for assignments and step locks.
$comment-exit1: known failure mode: writes a complete correct answer, then dies with a Console-sync auth error and exit 1. The verdict sets contentUsableDespiteExit instead of discarding the work.
$comment-preferredConcurrency: OpenCode's shared local/provider session can terminate sibling headless runs together under parallel load. Prefer one in-flight OpenCode worker and route other ready siblings to healthy pools; if no alternative is eligible, availability wins and OpenCode may still be used.
$comment-reasoning: verified 2026-09-09 against opencode 1.18.25: `opencode run --help` documents `--variant  model variant (provider-specific reasoning effort, e.g., high, max, minimal)`. opencode only forwards a variant its CONFIG declares for that model, and a stock opencode.json declares none, so on a bare install `--variant` is accepted and silently dropped. The level reaches the API as `reasoning_effort` only when the config declares the five variants for that model; a provider that clones this template declares them through env.OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT, which the provider kit builds with opencodeVariants(providerId, models). Probed with that variable set: `--variant bogus` (reasoningEffort bogus-level) failed at the API with `level "bogus-level" not supported, valid levels: low, medium, high, xhigh, max`, and `--variant max` succeeded; probed again with the flag AFTER the positional task text, exactly where bullswarm appends it (`opencode run --auto --model <providerId>/<model> <task> --variant <level> --format json`), with the same API rejection for the bogus level, so the position is proven too. UNVERIFIED for opencode providers with no declared variants: the flag is a no-op there rather than an error.
$comment-pricing: No OpenCode relay model profile here has an authoritative public token rate card as of 2026-09-20 (kaihk/* and opencode/union-alpha were checked). Pricing is intentionally omitted so transcript token totals remain unknown-cost rather than being treated as zero; the underlying OpenAI card is not assigned to an unidentified relay.
$comment-timeout: No implicit wall-clock timeout; callers may opt in with --timeout or workflow step.timeoutSec
